description: Build the read-only EDGAR acquirer offline: the SGML acceptance-time parser, the cache layout and repository-policy guard, the append-only manifest writer and the acquirer itself, with synthetic-fixture tests
data_version: not applicable - no data was fetched; all fixtures are synthetic
outcome: completed
decision: The acquisition pipeline is implemented and unit-tested, so the moment authorisation arrives the pipeline runs from committed code rather than being written from scratch
key_finding: The acceptance-time parser handles both US daylight-saving transition days explicitly: a local time in the spring-forward 23-hour day is quarantined as nonexistent, and a local time in the fall-back 25-hour day is quarantined as ambiguous with BOTH candidate UTC readings recorded. Neither is ever silently resolved or defaulted to an assumed offset. The submissions-JSON acceptanceDateTime field is refused as a source because it mixes UTC and Eastern clock readings (S-41).
notes: 48 new tests; 115 in total, all passing; ZERO network calls in the test suite (the transport is injected and the rate limiter runs on an injected clock). The acquirer refuses to run without a declared User-Agent, caps requests at 2 per second, honours Retry-After with a bounded retry budget, and records every retrieval - successful or not - in an append-only JSONL manifest with the SHA-256 of the raw bytes. No filing archive was harvested, no paid data was pulled, no GitHub Actions run was started and .github/workflows/main.yml was not modified (D-006). The raw cache root is refused if it lies inside the repository working tree (D-015).

description: Close the two named verification gaps on the critical path: the day-level UK legal adoption instrument date for IFRS 15 and IFRS 16, and the day-level ASU 2016-01 issuance date; add the missing EV-202 row
data_version: research/event_calendar.csv (8 rows); research/source_ledger.csv S-55 to S-59
sample: not applicable - dated primary instruments, no return is computed
outcome: completed
decision: The UK dates are primary-verified against SI 2015/980 and the EU endorsement chain; ASU 2016-01 is primary-verified against the ASU's own document text - and its effective date is CORRECTED, moving the event one year earlier
key_finding: The UK legal instrument is The Companies, Partnerships and Groups (Accounts and Reports) Regulations 2015 (SI 2015/980), made 26 March 2015 and in force 6 April 2015; regulation 2(2) gives the mandatory date (financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2016) and the directors' early-application arm (financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2015). The UK required NO new instrument for IFRS 16, so its T-A is inherited from the EU endorsement (2017-10-31) and is flagged as a weaker anchor. ASU 2016-01 was issued 2016-01-05 and is effective for public business entities for fiscal years beginning after 2017-12-15 - the event calendar previously carried 2018-12-15, a date that belongs to ASU 2016-02 (EV-102), so EV-103 moves one year earlier.
notes: Decision D-016. Direct fetches of fasb.org return HTTP 403 in this environment, so the ASU text was read through the search provider's rendering and is corroborated independently by the FASB's own ASU 2018-03. Still OPEN: whether the UK filing route publishes a filing TIME and not only a date (the FCA NSM API host answered HTTP 403 to every request here); T-R needs a timestamp. No outcome-period return has been computed or inspected, so nothing downstream is affected by the EV-103 shift.

description: Register v1.2 of the hypothesis, the specification and the preregistration for the prospective holdout arm PH-1 (the IFRS 18 first-application window)
sample: not applicable - a registration, not an estimate
outcome: completed
decision: PH-1 is registered on 2026-10-22, before the first IFRS 18 report can be published in the 2027 interim reporting season, and no element of v1.1 is changed
key_finding: Four things are settled in advance, all of them narrowings. The IFRS 18 adopter-type contrast is settled in the negative, because the instruments converge on one application date and first-time IFRS adopters apply the IFRSs all at once (S-54), so PH-1 is a weaker and narrower test than the retrospective panel. The pre-emption arm becomes the real thing, because IFRS 18 carries a mandated IAS 8.30/.31 pre-adoption impact disclosure (S-49) and therefore a real pre-disclosure anchor T-PRE. The expected cluster count is stated in advance and is BELOW the minimum (approximately 3 to 10 against 12), so the PH-1 primary estimand is expected to be inconclusive by construction, and the inference is fixed in advance to the jurisdiction-level randomisation test and the wild-cluster bootstrap. The reporting discipline is once-only, and a peek voids the arm.
notes: Decision D-019. The previous handoff suggested the v1.2 registration would be E-015; the numbering here is chronological, so the earlier steps of the same session took E-015 to E-017 and the registration took E-018. Registering PH-1 does not unblock anything and licenses no result; it removes the possibility that the promotable test will be designed after the outcome exists. The v1.0 and v1.1 files are byte-identical to their previous versions.
